_comment: Measured counts for the two backend suites. Never inferred, never copied from a report — run the suite and read the literal `Tests:` line. Checked by `npm run floor` (scripts/check-test-floor.cjs). A floor may RISE on a green land and must never be lowered to make a red suite pass.
_why_three: `npm test`, `test:rules` and `test:e2e` gate three DIFFERENT SURFACES and move independently, so they are three numbers. `npm test` reads src/*.ts logic, driving the callables against a hand-written fake firestore. `test:rules` judges firestore.rules policy over documents the test itself seeded. `test:e2e` runs the real callables against a real emulator and then reads the documents THEY wrote back through the rules. One combined number would let a drop in one hide behind a rise in another. 🔴 THE THIRD ENTRY EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST TWO WERE BOTH GREEN WHILE NOTHING HAD EVER PROVEN THE FAMILY FEATURE WORKED — the same shape as `make check-deployed` (#431), which was added when deployment turned out to be a surface with no number at all.

unit.note: Written by check-test-floor.cjs --record on 2026-09-14. 1688/75 -> 1694/75, measured by `npm test` on 153850e, which is an ANCESTOR of origin/main — git show reproduces it. A floor may RISE and may never be lowered; this writer refuses a drop rather than recording one.

rules.note: Written by check-test-floor.cjs --record on 2026-09-14. 241/1 -> 241/1, measured by `npm run test:rules` on 153850e, which is an ANCESTOR of origin/main — git show reproduces it. A floor may RISE and may never be lowered; this writer refuses a drop rather than recording one.
rules.requires: NOTHING SPECIAL, as of W2-95 (2026-08-16) — `npm run test:rules` runs in a stock shell. It goes through scripts/with-jdk.cjs, which resolves a JDK 21+ even when it is an UNLINKED Homebrew keg that /usr/libexec/java_home cannot enumerate, and it passes --config ../firebase.rules.json so it starts its own emulator on 8282 (hub 4403, logging 4503) instead of the 8080 firebase.json pins. 🔴 BEFORE THAT IT WAS NOT MERELY AWKWARD, IT WAS UNRUNNABLE: emulators:exec STARTS an emulator and cannot attach to one, so with a dev emulator holding 8080 the gate exited 1 with `Could not start Firestore Emulator, port taken` — and with the default java at 19 it exited 1 even earlier, on `firebase-tools no longer supports Java version before 21`. Two independent blockers, each hiding the other. The old advice here (`run with JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21`) fixed only the second and is no longer needed.

e2e.note: Written by check-test-floor.cjs --record on 2026-09-14. 146/9 -> 146/9, measured by `npm run test:e2e` on 153850e, which is an ANCESTOR of origin/main — git show reproduces it. A floor may RISE and may never be lowered; this writer refuses a drop rather than recording one.
e2e.requires: NOTHING SPECIAL, as of W2-95 (2026-08-16) — same with-jdk.cjs wrapper as the rules gate. 📌 IT DOES NOT USE THE STANDARD PORTS: firebase.e2e.json puts firestore on 8181 and auth on 9198 precisely so this gate can run while a dev `emulators:start` holds 8080/9099. ⚠️ THE OLD NOTE HERE CLAIMED THIS SUITE THEREFORE "STARTS CLEANLY EVERY TIME", AND THAT WAS FALSE IN A STOCK SHELL: the port fix never addressed the JDK, so with the default java at 19 this gate exited 1 on `firebase-tools no longer supports Java version before 21`, exactly like the rules gate — measured 2026-08-16. Surviving ONE of two independent blockers reads as surviving both, right up until somebody runs it without a prepared shell.
